speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance of the skin lesion on your chest, including its size, color, and any changes you've noticed recently.

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that description; does the lesion have a rough, scaly texture or a pearly, translucent appearance with visible blood vessels? Additionally, have you noticed any ulceration or crusting in the center of the spot?

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest skin lesion close-up.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute appendicitis is anatomically impossible as a cause of a chest skin lesion; the patient is likely experiencing Squamous Cell Carcinoma or Basal Cell Carcinoma. The previous diagnosis was incorrect. Please confirm if the lesion is firm, fixed to underlying tissue, or has rolled borders, and request a biopsy.
